raw_case_text:
A previously healthy 20-year-old male patient presented with intermittent headaches, nausea and vomiting for 13 days, which had worsened in the previous 2 days. He also presented fever the day before the hospital admission. He took no regular medication. Physical examination revealed cervical rigidity, lymph node enlargements on the right side of the neck. Vital signs (body temperature, pulse rate, respiration rate, and blood pressure) were normal. Relevant laboratory tests and examinations were performed after admission. Complete blood count was normal (Hb 130 g/L, Leucocytes 3.9 x 109/L, with 1.4 x 109 lymphocytes/L, 1.6 x 109 neutrophils/L, 0.5 x 109 eosinophils/L, and 0.4 x 109 monocytes/L, and platelets 125 x 109/L), and the patient tested negative for HIV. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed hyperintensity in the bilateral frontopolar and parietal cortex and sulcus. A lumbar puncture revealed elevated CSF opening pressure (>330 mmH2O), decreased glucose (1.19 mmol/L), elevated protein (0.96 g/L), and pleocytosis of 358 x 106 leucocytes/L (91% eosinophils, 4% lymphocytes, 4% monocytes, and 1% plasma cells) (Figure 1A). Alcian blue staining revealed Cryptococcus (Figure 1B), and the CSF culture grew Cryptococcus neoformans resistant to fluconazole. To search for the cause of eosinophilia, metagenomic next-generation sequencing (m-NGS) of the CSF was performed, and only Cryptococcus neoformans (sequence number: 1427) was identified; no parasites or other pathogens were found. The patient was diagnosed with cryptococcal meningitis on the basis of his clinical symptoms and signs combined with the presence of Cryptococcus in the CSF. The following examinations were performed to identify the cause of lymph node enlargements. Color Doppler ultrasound of the superficial lymph nodes revealed multiple lymph node enlargements in the bilateral neck, axilla, and right groin. Chest computed tomography (CT) showed multiple lymph node enlargements on both sides of the neck, mediastinum, and lung hilum. A biopsy of the cervical lymph node was performed, and the pathological diagnosis was lymphocyte-rich cHL. An 18F-FDG PET-CT was performed and documented hypermetabolic activity on supra- and infra-diaphragmatic adenopathies, spleen and bone, corresponding to the stage IV of the Lugano classification. CSF analysis by flow cytometry showed no malignant cells.
Treatment for HL may suppress immunity and thus aggravate cryptococcal infection, and lymphocyte-rich cHL has an indolent biological nature; therefore, we first administered antifungal induction therapy (liposomal amphotericin B plus 5-flucytosine) and performed successive lumbar punctures to control the high CSF opening pressure. After 8 weeks, the symptoms of meningitis significantly improved. The CSF leukocyte count (8 x 106/L) and proportion of eosinophils (42%) were reduced, and a CSF culture was negative. The patient thus initiated antifungal consolidation therapy with voriconazole and was transferred to the hematology department to start chemotherapy with the ABVD protocol (doxorubicin, bleomycin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine). At the present moment, the patient has received antifungal consolidation therapy for 13 weeks and 4 cycles of ABVD and he is asymptomatic. CSF culture is still negative, and the leucocyte count and proportion of eosinophils in the CSF have decreased gradually with treatment (Figure 2).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 20-year-old previously healthy male presented with a 13-day history of intermittent headaches, nausea, and vomiting that worsened over the preceding 2 days, accompanied by a 1-day history of fever.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the 13 days prior to admission, the patient experienced intermittent headaches, nausea, and vomiting that acutely worsened 2 days before presentation, followed by fever the day before admission.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for headache, nausea, vomiting, fever, and right cervical lymphadenopathy.

objective.physical_examination: Normal vital signs; cervical rigidity (neck stiffness) and enlarged right-sided cervical lymph nodes.
objective.routine_investigations: Normal CBC: hemoglobin 130 g/L, WBC 3.9 x 10^9/L (1.6 x 10^9/L neutrophils, 1.4 x 10^9/L lymphocytes, 0.5 x 10^9/L eosinophils, 0.4 x 10^9/L monocytes), platelets 125 x 10^9/L; HIV test was negative. Superficial lymph node Doppler ultrasound showed multiple enlarged bilateral cervical, axillary, and right inguinal lymph nodes.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain MRI revealed hyperintensity in the bilateral frontopolar and parietal cortices and sulci. Lumbar puncture showed opening pressure >330 mmH2O, marked eosinophilic pleocytosis with WBC 358 x 10^6/L (91% eosinophils, 4% lymphocytes, 4% monocytes, 1% plasma cells), low glucose 1.19 mmol/L, elevated protein 0.96 g/L, negative CSF flow cytometry for malignancy, positive CSF Alcian blue stain, CSF culture isolating fluconazole-resistant Cryptococcus neoformans, and CSF mNGS detecting 1427 sequences of C. neoformans with no parasites. Chest CT and 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated hypermetabolic supra- and infradiaphragmatic lymphadenopathy with splenic and bone involvement (Lugano stage IV), and cervical lymph node biopsy confirmed lymphocyte-rich classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis of eosinophilic Cryptococcus neoformans meningitis (with primary fluconazole resistance) unmasking newly diagnosed stage IV lymphocyte-rich classical Hodgkin lymphoma, confirmed by CSF Alcian blue staining, CSF fungal culture, CSF mNGS (1427 reads of C. neoformans, excluding parasitic eosinophilic meningitis), and cervical lymph node biopsy/PET-CT staging. Because chemotherapy would worsen fungal immunosuppression, he first received 8 weeks of antifungal induction with liposomal amphotericin B plus 5-flucytosine and serial therapeutic lumbar punctures (reducing CSF WBC to 8 x 10^6/L [42% eosinophils] and sterilizing CSF cultures), followed by consolidation therapy with oral voriconazole alongside 4 cycles of ABVD chemotherapy, remaining asymptomatic with negative CSF cultures at 13 weeks of consolidation.
